alice-eng: Hey team, hitting a weird intermittent 403 on the canary deploy job (gitlab 'deploy-canary'). ~1 in 5 runs fail with:
`HTTP 403` + JSON: {"error":"insufficient_scope", "required_scope":"deploy:write"}. Only on our self-hosted runners, same SA used everywhere. Any ideas?

ben-support: Can you paste the failing curl output and the auth header (redact token)? Also which runner image?

alice-eng: Pasted below (redacted token). Runner image: runner-ubuntu-22.04.
```
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.example/v1/deploys/canary
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="deploy:write"
{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token missing required scope: deploy:write"}
```

alice-eng: The token is minted by our internal token-exchange (exchange-service) which caches tokens for short windows. This started after we rolled out exchange-service v2 (cache enabled by default).

sara-sre: Two quick checks: 1) Are tokens minted with the right scopes? 2) Is there any proxy or cache returning an older token copy?

alice-eng: 1) Yes, mint logs show scopes include `deploy:write`. 2) We have token-cache-proxy in front of exchange-service. It returns cached token objects. I can dump the mint metadata if helpful.

ben-support: Please paste the mint log for a failing run (timestamps close to the request). We want `issued_at` and `expires_at` values.

alice-eng: Here is a failing sequence (times redacted a bit):
```
[exchange-service] issued token id=abc123 for sa=ci-deployer scopes=[deploy:write] issued_at=1670000000 expires_in=60
[token-cache-proxy] cache SET key=sa:ci-deployer value=abc123 ttl=30
[runner] request -> proxy returns token abc123 (age=30s) -> call to redwood api -> 403 insufficient_scope
```

alice-eng: So proxy TTL < token lifetime; proxy returned a token at ~30s old. Could that lead to scope loss? Weird.

deploy-bot: [automated] token-introspect for token=abc123 => active=true scopes=[deploy:write] exp=1670000060

ben-support: That log shows the token is still active and scopes are correct. However, some auth stacks reject tokens close to expiry if `exp` is within a safety margin (e.g., < 15s remaining). Do our Redwood API frontends check for a safety margin?

jordan-plat: Yes, we have a hard-coded safety margin on token acceptance: we reject tokens with <10s TTL to avoid mid-request expiry during streaming. If exchange-service issues tokens with 60s lifetime and proxy caches them for 30s, a request served near the cache edge could have <30s left. That shouldn't trigger scope removal, but if the exchange-service rotated the token id and our role binding logic maps scopes by token id in a short-lived cache, there could be a race.

ben-support: Two hypotheses: (A) token-cache-proxy is returning a token object whose internal metadata (scopes) expired in our local cache entry (stale metadata mapping), or (B) the exchange-service briefly emitted tokens without the `deploy:write` scope due to a race when policy backend refreshes.

alice-eng: Can reproduce reliably in local: launch proxy with TTL=30, mint token (60s), wait 28s, make request -> 403. If I disable cache (TTL=0) everything passes.

sara-sre: Repro is good. Next step: capture the exact Authorization header and the token introspect at the moment of request failure. Also check exchange-service logs for any scope-change events.

ben-support: I pulled proxy code — it caches only the raw token string but lazily refreshes metadata asynchronously. If the metadata refresh fails, the proxy keeps returning the token string but without updated `scopes` metadata attached in its local index. Edge-case: proxy SET ttl shorter than token lifetime, then async metadata refresh hasn't completed -> metadata lookup returns nil -> token appears to have no scopes.

alice-eng: Oh wow. That matches. The returned token is legit, but proxy's metadata cache can be nil and then our platform treats tokens without metadata as least-privileged -> yields insufficient_scope.

jordan-plat: Root cause: token-cache-proxy v1.3 introduced async metadata fetch to reduce latency but didn't guarantee metadata is populated before serving cached tokens. When TTLs are small this race shows.

ops-oncall: Proposed fixes: 1) Force proxy to block until metadata available on cache miss, or 2) have proxy set cache TTL >= token lifetime - safety_margin, or 3) platform should fallback to introspect upstream on metadata-miss rather than using empty metadata. Which should we patch first?

ben-support: Quickest patch is (3) — make platform call exchange-service introspect when metadata missing. Low-risk change. I'll open a hotfix.

jordan-plat: I'll also change proxy defaults: set `DEFAULT_CACHE_TTL = max(token.expires_in - 15, 30)` and add a flag `ENSURE_METADATA=true` for the proxy. We'll roll that in the next release.

alice-eng: Hotfix deployed to prod (platform introspect fallback). Retried 10 canaries: 10/10 success. Rolling to rest of canaries now.

ops-oncall: Patch deployed to proxy in staging with new defaults; we'll schedule prod roll tomorrow after monitoring window.

ben-support: Closing root-cause: token-cache-proxy async-metadata race when cache TTL < token lifetime led to token served without attached scope metadata, causing platform to treat token as least-privilege -> 403 insufficient_scope. Fix: platform fallback to introspect + proxy default TTL change + optional metadata enforcement.

alice-eng: Thanks all :thumbsup: Saved our deploys. Follow-up: we'll align token lifetimes and cache TTL strategy (ops doc) and add unit test for metadata race.

ops-oncall: Filed follow-up doc: https://go.internal/docs/ci-token-cache-guidelines (internal).
